Formula 1 returns to Austin's Circuit of The Americas for the United States Grand Prix with a historic championship crowning potentially in the offing, along with several other hot topics on the agenda. messages.text: What next for Kartal after 'unbelievable week' in Wuhan

metadata.summary: Sonay Kartal is the new British No 1 after her remarkable run to the Wuhan Open final where she was narrowly beaten by Poland's Maja Chwalinska in three sets.
metadata.content: Sonay Kartal: What next for new British No 1 after 'unbelievable week' in run to the final at Wuhan Open | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Sonay Kartal: What next for new British No 1 after 'unbelievable week' in run to the final at Wuhan Open Britain's Sonay Kartal enjoyed the best week of her career so far as she surprisingly made the final at the Wuhan Open; Kartal only recently returned from injury, so what is her potential and can she kick on? Watch the Japan Open all this week, live on Sky Sports Tennis Nigel Chiu Sports Journalist @NigelCJourno Sunday 18 October 2026 17:27, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Wuhan Open final between Sonay Kartal and Maja Chwalinska. Sonay Kartal is the new British No 1 after her remarkable run to the Wuhan Open final where she was narrowly beaten by Poland's Maja Chwalinska in three sets. Kartal became just the second Briton, after Johanna Konta, to play in a WTA 1000 final with superb wins over Tokyo Olympic champion Belinda Bencic, two-time Grand Slam finalist Jasmine Paolini, world No 6 Elina Svitolina and former French Open champion Jelena Ostapenko. It is arguably the most impressive tournament performance from a British female player since Emma Raducanu won the 2021 US Open, particularly given Kartal only returned to action last month following six months out due to a stress fracture in her back. metadata.content: Daniel Dubois vs Moses Itauma is an all-British heavyweight rivalry for the future | 'British boxing's in a great position' | Boxing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Analysis Daniel Dubois vs Moses Itauma is an all-British heavyweight rivalry for the future | 'British boxing's in a great position' Daniel Dubois scored a stunning two-round victory in Saturday's rematch with Fabio Wardley to defend the WBO heavyweight world title; Moses Itauma has to rebuild from his IBF world championship defeat to Filip Hrgovic but can return to set himself on a collision course with Dubois John Dennen Sports Journalist @johndennen Monday 19 October 2026 06:06, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the WBO heavyweight rematch between Daniel Dubois and Fabio Wardley (Video courtesy of DAZN) Daniel Dubois and Moses Itauma could become the heavyweight rivalry to define British boxing in the years to come. The sport in the UK has been dominated by the personalities and talents of Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury over the last decade. Although Fury and Joshua didn't box each other when they were both reigning world champions, they will finally fight in December in Cardiff. That really will be a swansong bout for Fury and Joshua. While it's hard to imagine Dubois and Itauma matching the levels of fame Fury and AJ enjoyed, they can emulate them as two British rivals taking over the top of the heavyweight division.
